short_description: Binucleate flagellated protozoan (genus Giardia, also called G. duodenalis / G. intestinalis) whose bilaterally symmetric, teardrop-shaped trophozoite (~12-15 x 5-9 um) carries two symmetric anterior nuclei giving it a famously face-like look, a large concave ventral adhesive disc that clamps onto small-intestinal enterocytes, a median body of microtubules, and eight flagella in four bilateral pairs (anterior, posterolateral, ventral, caudal); it does not invade tissue but coats the mucosa, blunts villi and interferes with fat/vitamin absorption, and encysts into an oval four-nucleated environmentally resistant cyst that is shed in faeces and survives in untreated water, making it the classic 'backpacker's/beaver fever' waterborne diarrhoeal parasite.

colour_legend.cell_body: warm translucent ivory-tan cytoplasm (SEM: false-colour pale gold/tan surface, since a live trophozoite has no pigment of its own)
colour_legend.nuclei: soft violet-blue, paired and symmetric either side of the midline (the 'eyes')
colour_legend.karyosome: small deeper indigo dot centred in each nucleus
colour_legend.ventral_disc: muted teal-grey concave spiral ridge on the flat ventral face
colour_legend.median_body: dusty rose curved bundle, claw-hammer shaped, midline dorsal to the caudal axonemes
colour_legend.axonemes_flagella: pale amber-cream flexible cords, eight in four pairs
colour_legend.cyst_wall: pale straw-yellow thick fibrillar wall (when the cyst is shown)
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (watercolour: warm aged cream paper)
colour_legend.note: A single protozoan cell is essentially colourless/translucent; SEM images false-colour, and a live trophozoite would be optically near-transparent under light microscopy. Colour here is a teaching convention (see reference/colors.md), not the organism's real colour. Keep this same structure->colour mapping across textbook, sem, 3d and watercolor so the set reads as one poster.

labels.en: Trophozoite body - bilaterally symmetric, teardrop/pear-shaped, dorsally convex & ventrally flat
labels.de: Trophozoit - birnen-/tropfenförmig, bilateral symmetrisch, dorsal konvex, ventral flach

labels.en: Left nucleus, with a central karyosome - one of the two symmetric 'eyes'
labels.de: Linker Zellkern (mit Karyosom) - eines der zwei symmetrischen 'Augen'

labels.en: Right nucleus, with a central karyosome - mirror image of the left
labels.de: Rechter Zellkern (mit Karyosom) - Spiegelbild des linken

labels.en: Ventral adhesive (sucker) disc - concave spiral of microtubules that clamps onto the intestinal wall
labels.de: Ventrale Haftscheibe (Saugscheibe) - konkave Mikrotubuli-Spirale, die sich an der Darmwand festsaugt

labels.en: Median body - claw-hammer-shaped microtubule bundle on the midline, a diagnostic feature
labels.de: Medianer Körper - hammerförmiges Mikrotubuli-Bündel auf der Mittellinie, ein diagnostisches Merkmal

labels.en: Caudal flagella pair - trailing from the tapered posterior tip
labels.de: Kaudales Geißelpaar - von der verjüngten Hinterspitze ausgehend

labels.en: Cyst - oval, thick-walled, four-nucleated resting/transmission stage shed in stool
labels.de: Zyste - ovale, dickwandige Dauerform mit vier Zellkernen, die mit dem Stuhl ausgeschieden wird

do_not_draw: a SINGLE nucleus, or asymmetric/off-centre nuclei - the two nuclei must be a mirror-image pair either side of the midline, both visible together giving the face-like look
an amoeba with pseudopods, blobby shape-shifting outline, or crawling amoeboid motion - Giardia keeps a fixed bilaterally symmetric pear/teardrop outline, it does not flow or extend pseudopods
a ciliate covered in a dense short fuzzy coat of cilia all over the body (that is Paramecium/Balantidium) - Giardia has exactly EIGHT discrete long flagella in four pairs, not a ciliated surface
more or fewer than eight flagella on the trophozoite (four pairs: anterior, posterolateral, ventral, caudal) - the count is a checkable diagnostic fact
a bacterial cell wall, peptidoglycan layer, capsule, pilus or nucleoid - Giardia is a eukaryote with a nuclear membrane, not a bacterium
a virus capsid, icosahedral shell or envelope with spikes - Giardia is a single-celled eukaryotic protozoan, not a virus

mitochondria (Giardia is amitochondriate/has only reduced mitosomes - do not draw prominent classical mitochondria) or a large single Golgi stack (Giardia's Golgi is minimal/absent in the trophozoite)
an asymmetric, lopsided or radially symmetric body plan - the defining feature is BILATERAL symmetry down the long axis
the adhesive disc drawn as a flat sticky pad or suction cup with no internal spiral microtubule structure, or placed on the dorsal (convex) instead of ventral (flat) surface

a flat two-dimensional silhouette with no dorsal/ventral distinction - the dorsal surface is convex (domed) and the ventral surface is flat/concave, and this difference should be readable in 3D renders
baked-in text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars or watermarks
a black border, dark frame, vignette, letterbox bar, mat, drop shadow, or the artwork drawn as a sheet/card lying on a surface

reference.note: A single, cleanly isolated Giardia lamblia trophozoite on a plain black background - textbook example, no clumping. Clearly shows the pear/teardrop outline, the concave ventral face with the adhesive-disc depression, and multiple long trailing flagella (some looped near the body, several trailing free posteriorly) against empty background. Greyscale (not false-colored) SEM, no baked-in text or scale bar, no border - used AS-IS (no edit_image.py pass) per the pipeline rule to skip cleanup when there is nothing to clean; a plain resize/crop is deterministic and truthful. Only mild imperfection: because several flagella overlap/loop near the body it is hard to count all eight individually in this single frame, though the four-pairs anatomy is described accurately in the label set from the literature.
